Subject: Azure marketplace technical intake — checklist and minimums

Olivia / Jason — following today's intake, here's the technical checklist and the minimum artifacts we'll need from Contoso to move the Azure listing and co-sell metadata forward. I'm keeping this focused so your infra and product teams can action quickly.

Required publisher-account items (publisher admin must provide):
- MPN ID and Publisher Profile URL (Marketplace publisher center).
- Primary technical contact + billing contact email.
- Service Principal (app registration) with Contributor role in the publisher tenant for automated offer submission (we can also do manual upload if policy prevents SPNs).

Offer payload & manifest items (we need these files/values):
- Offer name, summary (1-2 sentences), long description, category tags.
- SKU definitions for billing (monthly, hourly, usage unit) and canonical price tiers for co-sell mapping.
- Endpoint type: managed SaaS (we'll need the SaaS API callback URL) or BYOL/VM/container.
- Container image size / startup time estimates (if using container offer) and required outbound/inbound IP ranges.

Technical validation checklist (ops/security):
- Public TLS endpoint and a health-check path returning 200 within 10s.
- Authentication: OAuth2 / OIDC-compatible tokens or Azure AD integrations; sample auth flow and token validation endpoint.
- Telemetry: logs and basic metrics (token usage, 4xx/5xx rates) accessible via agreed channel (SAS link or workspace).
- Data handling: clear doc on data retention and controls for customer data; specify whether KV-cache or persistent storage is used.
- PrivateLink & VNet injection: confirm whether PrivateLink is required and supply required service alias (if applicable).

Co-sell metadata we will set (please provide values):
- Regions supported (US, EU, APAC).
- SKUs to map to co-sell catalog and suggested GTM tags (e.g., "ISV:MarketplaceCoSell").
- Case studies or logos we can surface on the offer page.

Files I'm attaching: sample offer payload (azure-offer-payload-sample.json) and a short intake template. Please return the payload with your values filled and we'll validate the manifest before submission.

Notes on timelines: once we have the publisher artifacts + filled payload, we can run a technical smoke test and aim for submission to Azure within 7 business days (assuming no major identity gaps). If you need us to create a service principal on your behalf, we can walk through the minimal permissions required.

Attachments: azure-offer-payload-sample.json (payload stub)

--
Karthik Iyer
Marketplace Integrations — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Jason Li <jason.li@contoso.com>

Date: Thu, 13 Jan 2028 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure marketplace technical intake — checklist and minimums

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our infra team after reviewing the payload sample:
- Our service is deployed as a managed SaaS offering behind a private VNet. We plan to expose a proxy endpoint in a public subnet for Marketplace callbacks. Will that satisfy the health-check and telemetry needs?
- We are restricted from creating service principals with Contributor at publisher-level; can we instead provide an exportable manifest and allow Redwood to do the submission under your partner account and transfer ownership later?
- For co-sell mapping, can you share the exact SKU key format Azure expects? Our finance team wants to align line items exactly.

Also: attached is a marked-up intake sheet — highlighted sections where we need Redwood input on price-tier recommendations and recommended GTM tags.

Attachments: contoso-co-sell-intake.xlsx (updated)

Best,
Jason Li
Platform Engineer, Contoso Cloud Integrations

Subject: Re: Azure marketplace technical intake — checklist and minimums

Jason — quick answers and next steps.

1) Private VNet + public proxy: yes, that pattern is fine. For the smoke test we will hit the public proxy health endpoint and validate telemetry via a read-only SAS to your metrics workspace. Please provide the health path and expected response code.

2) Service principal alternative: yes — we can accept an exportable manifest and submit under the Redwood partner submission flow, then initiate an ownership transfer once validated. We'll need a signed publisher authorization form (PDF) and a contact who can approve transfer in the publisher center.

3) SKU key format: we'll send a short sample mapping to match Azure's expected schema (SKU key format: <offerId>.<skuId>.<meteringDimension>). Karthik will attach the exact snippet and price-tier guidance in a follow-up before COB tomorrow.

Action items / deadlines:
- Contoso: supply filled azure-offer-payload-sample.json, health-check URL, and signed publisher authorization by EOD Wed 1/19.
- Redwood: Karthik will provide SKU mapping snippet and price-tier suggestions by Tue 1/18.
- Schedule: Subject to timely delivery, aim to submit offer to Marketplace week of Jan 22.

I'll coordinate the DocuSign for the authorization form and share the submission link. Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
